_comment: hmbridge example configuration. Every object accepts an optional _comment field.

radio: auto (default; detected at startup), hm-mod-rpi-pcb or rpi-rf-mod. reset: gpio (the module's reset line on the Pi's header), raw-uart (OpenCCU's driver, for /dev/raw-uart), none, or auto (default). reset_gpio: BCM GPIO of the reset line, default 18 (HM-MOD-RPI-PCB) or 19 (RPI-RF-MOD), chosen at startup with radio auto.
Only central_address and devices are required; all other fields show their defaults or typical values.

http_listen serves the read-only JSON API (/api/v1/health, /bridge, /devices, /groups, /unknown; GET / lists them) and Prometheus /metrics ("" disables it; use 127.0.0.1:8013 to keep it local). Requests must name hmbridge: an IP address, localhost, the machine's host name (or <name>.local), or a name listed in http_allowed_hosts (e.g. ["hmbridge.example.lan"]). time_sync_interval: how often the radio module clock is set.

require_synced_clock (default true): only hand out the time while the system clock is NTP-synchronised. state_dir (absolute; "" disables persistence and pairing) holds hmbridge's files: state.json, the fallback for restoring device state when the MQTT broker is unreachable at startup, written only after significant changes, at most every state_save_interval, and on shutdown; and devices.json, the paired devices. On OpenCCU use /usr/local/hmbridge/state. state_file and devices_file are deprecated.

Every device accepts stale_after (e.g. "2h", "0s" = never): how long it may be silent before Home Assistant shows it as unavailable (default 30m thermostats, 1h weather sensors, 6h HM-Sec-SCo, 50h other contacts, 3 status_poll_interval for switches/dimmers/LED displays, never for remotes). For switches, dimmers and LED displays it must be longer than status_poll_interval.
status_poll_interval (default 1h, "0s" disables): how often switches, dimmers and the LED display are asked for their status; they are always asked once shortly after startup.

csma_ca enables listen-before-talk (default false, like the CCU). answer_time_requests (default true): set false if the radio module already answers the devices' time requests (duplicate 0x3F answers in the -debug log).

The CCU's system security key. Give one of passphrase (key = MD5(passphrase), as the CCU does), key (32 hex chars) or key_file (absolute path of a file holding the 32 hex chars, mode 0600; hmbridge init creates one with a new random key).
index is the key index shown by the CCU (1 after the first key change, incremented on every change). Default 1.
previous is optional: the key before the last change, needed while not all devices have been switched to the new key.
Omit the whole security block if you never set a key on your CCU (eQ-3 default key, index 0).

mqtt._comment: Set broker to "" to disable MQTT.

_comment: Defaults for heating groups and thermostats with "control": "home_assistant" (Home Assistant, e.g. the Advanced Heating Control blueprint, decides the target temperature; hmbridge keeps the thermostats in manual mode). See docs/DEPLOY.md, "Using Home Assistant for heating control".

fallback_after: fail-safe. When the MQTT connection (or Home Assistant itself) has been gone this long, the thermostats are switched to their own week program (auto mode); when it has been back for a minute, Home Assistant's last setpoint is sent again. Default 30m, "0s" disables the fallback, otherwise at least 5m. Groups and thermostats can override it with their own fallback_after.
setpoint_debounce: target temperatures from Home Assistant that follow each other within this time are merged; only the last one is sent (default 2s, "0s" sends each at once, at most 30s).

Pairing new devices from Home Assistant (button "Pair new device" on the hmbridge device; MQTT only, the HTTP API is read-only). Paired devices are kept in devices.json in state_dir, which is only written on pair, unpair and rename; on a conflict, devices below win.

aes: "system_key" (default when security is set) gives AES-capable devices the security key and enables AES where a CCU does (contacts, push buttons, remotes); "off" leaves them on the eQ-3 default key without AES.
duration: how long pairing mode stays on (10s … 10m).

_comment: A group mirrors a CCU heating group and becomes ONE climate entity in Home Assistant.
Members are device names or addresses; a device can be in at most one group; a group needs at least one thermostat.
Setpoint/mode commands are sent to all thermostats of the group: wall thermostats first, then radiator thermostats.
Current temperature/humidity come from the wall thermostat if present, else from the first radiator thermostat.
The window state comes from the contact(s): open if any contact is open or tilted.
Direct peerings between the devices (thermostat team, window contact) are left untouched and keep working without hmbridge.
via_wall_thermostat: send group commands only to the wall thermostat, which forwards them over its direct links (half the radio airtime). Default false.

In Home Assistant a group is a device "<name> (group)" with the climate entity (its attributes list the members), the window state, and per member: valve (radiator thermostats), temperature and humidity (wall thermostats), window (contacts), and a diagnostic availability sensor.

groups_suggest_area (top level, default true): suggest the group name as Home Assistant area for the group device and its members' devices. Home Assistant only applies it when it first creates a device.

control: "device" (default: the thermostats run their week program, Home Assistant can switch auto/heat/off) or "home_assistant" (Home Assistant sets the target temperature, the thermostats are kept in manual mode, with the fail-safe of home_assistant_control; fallback_after overrides its default for this group).
groups.name: Wohnzimmer
